exhibits.title: Mona Lisa
exhibits.description: A softly modeled portrait whose enigmatic expression and atmospheric landscape exemplify Leonardo's sfumato technique.

exhibits.title: The School of Athens
exhibits.description: Ancient philosophers gather in an idealized architectural space celebrating reason, mathematics and inquiry.

exhibits.title: Lady with an Ermine
exhibits.description: A young woman turns while holding an ermine, combining psychological presence with graceful movement.

exhibits.title: The Annunciation (San Marco fresco)
exhibits.description: Gabriel kneels before Mary beneath a simple arcaded loggia. The spare architecture, quiet gestures and soft color create a contemplative devotional scene.

exhibits.title: The Last Supper
exhibits.description: Christ announces his impending betrayal at a communal meal, while the apostles respond with dramatically varied gestures.

exhibits.title: Primavera
exhibits.description: Mythological figures assemble in a richly detailed grove, evoking spring, love and renewal.

exhibits.title: Sistine Madonna
exhibits.description: The Virgin and Child appear among clouds, accompanied by saints and two famous cherubs.
exhibits.credit: Google Art Project: Home - pic Maximum resolution.

exhibits.title: The Lamentation
exhibits.description: Mourners gather around Christ's body in an emotionally direct fresco that helped transform European painting.

exhibits.title: The Creation of Adam
exhibits.description: God and Adam reach toward one another in a fresco exploring creation and the origin of human life.

exhibits.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
exhibits.description: A richly furnished domestic interior uses a convex mirror, intricate objects and light to create layers of meaning.

exhibits.title: Venus of Urbino
exhibits.description: A reclining woman meets the viewer's gaze in a richly colored Venetian interior.

exhibits.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
exhibits.description: A young figure turns toward the viewer, with luminous fabric and an oversized pearl-like earring.

exhibits.title: The Milkmaid
exhibits.description: A servant pours milk in a quiet domestic scene distinguished by meticulous observation of light and texture.

exhibits.title: The Storm on the Sea of Galilee
exhibits.description: Christ and his disciples confront a turbulent sea in a dramatic study of faith and human vulnerability.

exhibits.title: The Supper at Emmaus
exhibits.description: Disciples recognize the risen Christ during a meal, their gestures heightening the moment of revelation.

exhibits.title: The Night Watch
exhibits.description: A civic guard company emerges in a dynamic group portrait distinguished by dramatic illumination.

exhibits.title: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
exhibits.description: Surgeons gather around a dissected arm, demonstrating anatomical observation and professional learning.

exhibits.title: The Swing
exhibits.description: A young woman swings through a lush garden in a playful scene associated with Rococo elegance.
exhibits.credit: The Trustees of the Wallace Collection

exhibits.title: The Art of Painting
exhibits.description: An artist paints an allegorical model in a carefully arranged studio, reflecting on the nature of painting.

exhibits.title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
exhibits.description: A shaft of light emphasizes the moment of Matthew's calling in a contemporary-looking interior.

exhibits.title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
exhibits.description: Judith and her maid overpower Holofernes in a dramatic rendering of the biblical story.

exhibits.title: The Elevation of the Cross
exhibits.description: Figures strain to raise the cross in a powerful composition defined by diagonals and muscular movement.

exhibits.title: The Rokeby Venus
exhibits.description: A reclining Venus looks toward a mirror held by Cupid in a study of beauty and reflected vision.

exhibits.title: Wanderer Above the Sea of Fog
exhibits.description: A solitary figure surveys a sea of fog, embodying the Romantic sublime and the unknowable scale of nature.

exhibits.title: The Death of Socrates
exhibits.description: Socrates faces death while continuing to teach, embodying philosophical conviction and intellectual courage.

exhibits.title: The Oath of the Horatii
exhibits.description: Three brothers pledge loyalty before their father, dramatizing civic duty and personal sacrifice.

exhibits.title: The Hay Wain
exhibits.description: A rural wagon crosses a shallow river in a detailed study of the English countryside.

exhibits.title: Liberty Leading the People
exhibits.description: An allegorical figure of Liberty leads revolutionaries over a barricade in a vision of political upheaval.

exhibits.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
exhibits.description: A mythological father consumes his child in a disturbing vision of fear, power and destruction.

exhibits.title: The Death of Marat
exhibits.description: The murdered revolutionary Jean-Paul Marat is depicted in a spare, idealized scene of political martyrdom.

exhibits.title: The Gleaners
exhibits.description: Three women collect leftover grain, making rural labor and social inequality the subject of monumental art.

exhibits.title: The Raft of the Medusa
exhibits.description: Shipwreck survivors struggle toward rescue in a monumental composition exploring suffering and hope.

exhibits.title: The Nightmare
exhibits.description: A sleeping woman and uncanny figures create a haunting meditation on dreams and terror.

exhibits.title: The Fighting Temeraire
exhibits.description: An aging warship is towed toward dismantling as sunset and steam power evoke historical change.

exhibits.title: The Ninth Wave
exhibits.description: Survivors face immense waves beneath a luminous sky in a dramatic image of nature's power.

exhibits.title: The Scream
exhibits.description: An anguished figure stands against a violently colored sky in an enduring image of existential anxiety.

exhibits.title: Café Terrace at Night
exhibits.description: A warmly illuminated café terrace contrasts with the deep blue of an evening street and sky.

exhibits.title: The Night Café
exhibits.description: An intensely colored café interior expresses unease through exaggerated perspective and contrasting hues.

exhibits.title: The Card Players (Musée d’Orsay version)
exhibits.description: Two men sit across a small table playing cards, with a bottle between them. Cézanne builds the composition from restrained color and solid geometric forms. This is the Musée d’Orsay version of the series.

exhibits.title: The Kiss
exhibits.description: Two embracing figures dissolve into intricate gilded ornament in a celebration of intimacy.

exhibits.title: Starry Night Over the Rhône
exhibits.description: Stars and artificial lights shimmer on the Rhône in a nocturnal study of reflected color.

exhibits.title: Wheatfield with Crows
exhibits.description: A turbulent sky, wheat fields and dark birds create a powerful late landscape.

exhibits.title: Impression, Sunrise
exhibits.description: A hazy harbor and orange sun capture the fleeting effect of atmosphere that gave Impressionism its name.

exhibits.title: Sunflowers (National Gallery version)
exhibits.description: A vase of sunflowers in varied stages of bloom stands against a yellow background. This is the 1888 London National Gallery version (NG3863), one of Van Gogh’s series of sunflower still lifes.

exhibits.title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
exhibits.description: Friends gather around a table on a sunny terrace in an intimate study of social life and color.

exhibits.title: Nighthawks
exhibits.description: Late-night customers occupy a brightly lit diner surrounded by an empty urban street.

exhibits.title: American Gothic
exhibits.description: A stern pair stands before a Gothic-windowed house in an iconic image of rural American identity.

exhibits.title: Black Square
exhibits.description: A black square on a pale ground radically reduces painting to a nonrepresentational statement.

exhibits.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
exhibits.description: An enormous wave towers over boats and distant Mount Fuji in a celebrated Japanese woodblock print.

exhibits.title: Red Fuji
exhibits.description: Mount Fuji glows red beneath a patterned sky in one of Hokusai's celebrated woodblock views.

exhibits.title: The Tortoise Trainer
exhibits.description: A figure attends to tortoises in a tiled interior, a scene often interpreted in relation to reform and patience.

exhibits.title: Along the River During the Qingming Festival (city gate detail)
exhibits.description: This excerpt from Zhang Zeduan’s Song-dynasty handscroll shows a city gate and the activity surrounding it. The complete scroll traces daily life across rural and urban settings; only one section is reproduced here.

exhibits.title: Red and White Plum Blossoms
exhibits.description: Flowering trees flank a stylized stream across a pair of richly decorative Japanese screens.

exhibits.title: A Thousand Li of Rivers and Mountains (detail)
exhibits.description: A section of Wang Ximeng’s blue-green landscape handscroll, featuring layered mountain forms, water and inscriptions. The original is a long panoramic composition; this image is an excerpt.

exhibits.title: Shakuntala
exhibits.description: Shakuntala, a heroine of Sanskrit literature, turns back as her companions stand nearby in a wooded setting. The painting evokes the story of her love for King Dushyanta.

exhibits.title: Spoliarium
exhibits.description: Fallen gladiators are dragged into a Roman arena's service area in a monumental image of suffering and injustice.

exhibits.title: The Parisian Life
exhibits.description: A woman sits in a Parisian café near a group of men in an enigmatic scene of metropolitan life.

exhibits.title: Las Virgenes Cristianas Expuestas al Populacho
exhibits.description: Christian women face public humiliation in an academic historical painting of persecution.

exhibits.title: A Philosopher Lecturing on the Orrery
exhibits.description: A group watches a model of the solar system illuminated by an artificial sun, dramatizing Enlightenment curiosity.

exhibits.title: The Astronomer
exhibits.description: A scholar examines a celestial globe in a quiet interior devoted to astronomical study.

exhibits.title: The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus
exhibits.description: An alchemist encounters luminous phosphorus, making a historical discovery the focus of dramatic illumination.

exhibits.title: The Geographer
exhibits.description: A scholar pauses over maps and instruments in a study of observation and geographical knowledge.

exhibits.title: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
exhibits.description: Observers respond to an air-pump demonstration, raising questions about experimentation and scientific ethics.

exhibits.title: Portrait of the Lavoisiers
exhibits.description: The chemist Antoine Lavoisier and Marie-Anne Paulze Lavoisier appear with laboratory instruments, emphasizing scientific partnership.

exhibits.title: The Death of Socrates
exhibits.description: Socrates faces death while continuing to teach, embodying philosophical conviction and intellectual courage.

exhibits.title: Vitruvian Man
exhibits.description: Leonardo's pen-and-ink study places the human body inside a circle and square, connecting anatomy and geometry.

exhibits.title: Newton
exhibits.description: Newton bends over a geometric diagram with a compass, absorbed in measurement. Blake’s image can be read as a critique of a worldview restricted to rational calculation. It is a color print finished by hand, not a conventional oil portrait.

exhibits.title: Isaac Newton
exhibits.description: A portrait of the mathematician and physicist whose laws of motion and gravitation shaped classical mechanics.

artists.name: Zhang Zeduan
artists.biography: Zhang Zeduan is associated with the celebrated Qingming handscroll. Secure biographical information is limited; the work offers a densely observed panorama of urban and river life.
artists.context: A handscroll unfolds in stages, allowing the viewer to explore numerous incidents rather than a single fixed scene.

works.title: Along the River During the Qingming Festival (city gate detail)

artists.name: Wang Ximeng
artists.biography: Wang Ximeng is known for the monumental blue-and-green landscape handscroll A Thousand Li of Rivers and Mountains, dated 1113. Little is securely known of his life beyond the court context associated with the work.
artists.context: Mineral colors, layered mountain forms and the unfolding handscroll format create a vast imagined landscape.

works.title: A Thousand Li of Rivers and Mountains (detail)

artists.name: Giotto
artists.biography: Giotto helped transform Italian painting through substantial figures, spatial settings and emotionally direct storytelling. His fresco cycles became influential models for later painters.
artists.context: The Lamentation uses gestures and a shared direction of attention to express grief.

artists.name: Jan van Eyck
artists.biography: Van Eyck refined the expressive possibilities of oil painting, creating richly detailed surfaces and convincing reflections. He worked at the Burgundian court.
artists.context: Observe the mirror, textiles and tiny details in the Arnolfini Portrait.

artists.name: Fra Angelico
artists.biography: A Dominican friar and painter, Fra Angelico combined devotional imagery with emerging Renaissance approaches to space and light. His frescoes at San Marco in Florence were made for a religious community.
artists.context: Notice the quiet gestures, restrained architecture and contemplative use of color.

artists.name: Sandro Botticelli
artists.biography: Botticelli painted religious and mythological subjects in Florence. His graceful contours, rhythmic figures and poetic imagery reflect the city's humanist culture.
artists.context: Primavera invites attention to allegory, movement and the arrangement of figures.

artists.name: Leonardo da Vinci
artists.biography: Painter, engineer and investigator of nature, Leonardo treated observation and drawing as complementary tools. His studies of anatomy, optics and proportion connect painting with scientific inquiry.
artists.context: Look for soft transitions of light and shade (sfumato), natural gestures and carefully observed anatomy.

artists.name: Michelangelo
artists.biography: Michelangelo was a sculptor, painter and architect whose study of the human body shaped monumental works. His Sistine Chapel ceiling combines biblical narrative with complex figure compositions.
artists.context: The Creation of Adam uses the tension between two nearly touching hands as a visual focal point.

artists.name: Raphael
artists.biography: Raphael developed harmonious compositions combining classical architecture, idealized figures and clear spatial organization. He worked in Florence and Rome, including major Vatican fresco commissions.
artists.context: The School of Athens places philosophical inquiry within a balanced architectural setting.

artists.name: Titian
artists.biography: Titian became a leading Venetian painter, known for his portraits, mythological pictures and sophisticated color. His handling of paint grew increasingly free over his long career.
artists.context: Compare the warm flesh tones and fabric in Venus of Urbino with Florentine emphasis on line.

artists.name: Caravaggio
artists.biography: Caravaggio brought direct naturalism and strong contrasts of light into religious and narrative painting. His work influenced painters across Europe.
artists.context: Notice how a dramatic shaft of light and ordinary human gestures guide the narrative.

artists.name: Peter Paul Rubens
artists.biography: Rubens led a prominent Antwerp workshop and worked as a diplomat. His large altarpieces and mythological paintings are distinguished by energetic figures, color and movement.
artists.context: The Elevation of the Cross organizes the scene around a powerful diagonal.

artists.name: Artemisia Gentileschi
artists.biography: Gentileschi became an accomplished painter in a profession dominated by men. Her biblical and historical scenes often feature determined women, dramatic lighting and forceful action.
artists.context: Consider the physical effort and directional movement in her depiction of Judith.

artists.name: Diego Velázquez
artists.biography: Velázquez served as a painter at the Spanish royal court. His portraits and other subjects display an economical handling of paint and keen observation of space and appearance.
artists.context: The Rokeby Venus explores reflection, pose and the relationship between viewer and subject.

artists.name: Rembrandt
artists.biography: Rembrandt produced portraits, narrative paintings, drawings and prints. His expressive brushwork and contrast of light and shadow gave faces and scenes psychological depth.
artists.context: Compare the group portrait in The Night Watch with the intimate atmosphere of his other works.

works.title: The Storm on the Sea of Galilee
The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp

artists.name: Johannes Vermeer
artists.biography: Vermeer worked in Delft and is celebrated for carefully composed interiors and luminous effects. His paintings often transform everyday activities into quiet studies of light and attention.
artists.context: Compare window light, reflective surfaces and the geometry of his interior scenes.

artists.name: Godfrey Kneller
artists.biography: German-born Kneller became a prominent portrait painter in Britain, working for royal and aristocratic patrons as well as intellectual figures.
artists.context: His Newton portrait presents the scientist through the conventions of formal portraiture.

artists.name: Ogata Kōrin
artists.biography: Kōrin developed a highly decorative Japanese painting style using stylized natural motifs, bold design and lavish surfaces. His work is central to the tradition later called Rinpa.
artists.context: The plum blossom screens transform trees and water into rhythmic patterns.

artists.name: Jean-Honoré Fragonard
artists.biography: Fragonard painted playful, intimate and decorative scenes using energetic brushwork. His art belongs to the culture of eighteenth-century French Rococo.
artists.context: The Swing uses lush foliage, movement and a theatrical arrangement of figures.

artists.name: Joseph Wright of Derby
artists.biography: Wright made scientific demonstrations, industrial subjects and candlelit scenes central to his art. His paintings reflect eighteenth-century interest in experiment, observation and discovery.
artists.context: Compare the spectators and carefully staged light in his three scientific scenes.

works.title: A Philosopher Lecturing on the Orrery
An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump

artists.name: Henry Fuseli
artists.biography: Swiss-born Fuseli worked in Britain, painting literary, supernatural and imaginative subjects. His exaggerated figures and dramatic staging explore dreams and fear.
artists.context: The Nightmare combines familiar surroundings with unsettling supernatural imagery.

artists.name: Francisco Goya
artists.biography: Goya worked as a court painter while also making penetrating prints and images of violence, fear and social criticism. His late Black Paintings explore disturbing subjects.
artists.context: Saturn belongs to the late works made for the walls of his home, rather than a conventional public commission.

artists.name: Jacques-Louis David
artists.biography: David revived the visual language of classical antiquity in paintings of moral choice, politics and public life. His career spanned the French Revolution and the Napoleonic period.
artists.context: Compare the clear outlines, staged gestures and carefully organized groups in his historical scenes.

artists.name: William Blake
artists.biography: Blake was a poet, printmaker and painter who developed a personal symbolic universe. He often questioned the limits of narrowly rational explanations of human experience.
artists.context: Newton is a symbolic representation, not a documentary portrait of the scientist.

artists.name: Katsushika Hokusai
artists.biography: Hokusai was a Japanese print designer and painter whose subjects ranged from landscape to everyday life. His Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji became especially influential.
artists.context: Compare the dramatic cropping of The Great Wave with the simplified silhouette of Red Fuji.

artists.name: Caspar David Friedrich
artists.biography: Friedrich made landscapes that express solitude, contemplation and the encounter between humanity and nature. His figures often face away from the viewer toward expansive scenery.
artists.context: The wanderer becomes a stand-in for the viewer confronting the sublime landscape.

works.title: Wanderer Above the Sea of Fog

artists.name: J. M. W. Turner
artists.biography: Turner explored atmospheric light, weather and the changing relationship between nature and technology. His increasingly expressive landscapes influenced later painters.
artists.context: The Fighting Temeraire contrasts an old sailing warship with a steam-powered tug.

artists.name: John Constable
artists.biography: Constable painted the countryside of southern England with close attention to weather, clouds and familiar rural places. His outdoor studies informed ambitious finished landscapes.
artists.context: The Hay Wain rewards close attention to changing light and the relationship of water, sky and land.

artists.name: Théodore Géricault
artists.biography: Géricault pursued intense, contemporary subjects and studied anatomy and movement. His large paintings challenged conventional heroic history painting.
artists.context: The Raft of the Medusa turns a recent maritime disaster into a dramatic composition of desperation and hope.

artists.name: Eugène Delacroix
artists.biography: Delacroix used expressive color and dynamic compositions in historical, literary and political subjects. His approach became influential for later explorations of color.
artists.context: Liberty Leading the People uses an allegorical figure amid the upheaval of the July Revolution of 1830.

artists.name: Jean-François Millet
artists.biography: Millet made rural labor central to his art, lending dignity and monumentality to agricultural workers. He worked in Barbizon, near the forest of Fontainebleau.
artists.context: The Gleaners emphasizes repetitive labor through the bent figures and expansive harvest landscape.

artists.name: Ivan Aivazovsky
artists.biography: Aivazovsky, an Armenian painter born in the Russian Empire, became renowned for seascapes and the expressive depiction of waves and light.
artists.context: The Ninth Wave contrasts the danger of the sea with luminous atmospheric effects.

artists.name: Paul Cézanne
artists.biography: Cézanne investigated how color and simplified forms can construct pictorial space. His landscapes, still lifes and figure paintings influenced twentieth-century modernism.
artists.context: The Card Players reduces a familiar activity to a concentrated arrangement of shapes and tones.

artists.name: Claude Monet
artists.biography: Monet explored changing light and atmosphere through repeated observations of landscapes and everyday settings. He was a central figure in the Impressionist exhibitions.
artists.context: Impression, Sunrise emphasizes the fleeting effect of light over sharply defined detail.

artists.name: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
artists.biography: Renoir painted figures, portraits and scenes of social life with luminous color and a lively handling of paint. His later work increasingly emphasized solid figure forms.
artists.context: Luncheon of the Boating Party brings together varied gestures and interactions in a sunlit setting.

artists.name: Osman Hamdi Bey
artists.biography: An Ottoman painter, archaeologist and museum administrator, Osman Hamdi Bey helped establish institutions for art education and the preservation of antiquities. His paintings engage with historical architecture and cultural identity.
artists.context: The Tortoise Trainer sets a solitary figure within an intricately ornamented architectural space.

artists.name: Thomas Eakins
artists.biography: Eakins pursued precise observation of the human body through painting, drawing and photography. His portraits and scenes of medical and sporting activity reflect this interest.
artists.context: The Gross Clinic portrays surgery as an arena of professional skill and observation.

artists.name: Raja Ravi Varma
artists.biography: Ravi Varma combined European academic oil-painting techniques with subjects drawn from Indian literature, mythology and society. Reproductions of his work helped circulate these images widely.
artists.context: Shakuntala brings a literary narrative into a closely observed figurative scene.

artists.name: Vincent van Gogh
artists.biography: Van Gogh developed a distinctive language of intense color, directional brushwork and expressive observation. His landscapes, interiors and still lifes record the places and objects around him.
artists.context: Compare the emotional effects of color and brushwork in his night scenes and still lifes.

artists.name: Félix Resurrección Hidalgo
artists.biography: Hidalgo was a Filipino painter and contemporary of Juan Luna. His paintings include historical, literary and landscape subjects, and his work received recognition in European exhibitions.
artists.context: Observe how the arrangement of vulnerable figures communicates the violence of the scene.

works.title: Las Virgenes Cristianas Expuestas al Populacho

artists.name: Juan Luna
artists.biography: Luna trained and worked in Europe and became internationally recognized for ambitious historical paintings. His career is central to the history of nineteenth-century Philippine art.
artists.context: Compare the monumental Spoliarium with the more intimate Parisian Life.

artists.name: Gustav Klimt
artists.biography: Klimt helped found the Vienna Secession and developed a decorative visual language combining figures, pattern and symbolism. His golden-period paintings often blur the boundary between ornament and image.
artists.context: The Kiss contrasts geometric patterns and flowing decorative forms with intimate human figures.

artists.name: Leonid Pasternak
artists.biography: Pasternak was a painter and illustrator known for portraits and scenes of intellectual and cultural life. His works include images of prominent writers and thinkers.
artists.context: The Einstein portrait belongs to the museum's group of artistic interpretations of the physicist.

artists.name: Edvard Munch
artists.biography: Munch explored anxiety, love, illness and mortality through painting and printmaking. His expressive color and simplified forms helped shape modern art.
artists.context: The Scream turns psychological tension into a rhythmic landscape and figure.

artists.name: Vilma Lwoff-Parlaghy
artists.biography: Hungarian-born Lwoff-Parlaghy specialized in portraits of notable sitters. Her Blue Portrait of Nikola Tesla was shown in 1916 under specially arranged lighting.
artists.context: The distinctive blue cast connects portraiture with Tesla's interest in artificial illumination.

artists.name: Kazimir Malevich
artists.biography: Malevich developed Suprematism, an approach to non-objective art based on elementary forms and color. He sought to move painting beyond representation.
artists.context: Black Square makes the painted geometric form itself the subject of attention.

artists.name: Edward Hopper
artists.biography: Hopper painted urban and rural American settings, often using architecture and light to create a sense of isolation or suspended narrative.
artists.context: Nighthawks juxtaposes a brightly lit diner with the surrounding night streets.

artists.name: Erich Büttner
artists.biography: Büttner was a German painter and graphic artist whose work includes portraits of prominent contemporaries. His Einstein portrait records the physicist during the early period of relativity's reception.
artists.context: The portrait provides a human counterpart to the abstract ideas associated with Einstein.

artists.name: Grant Wood
artists.biography: Wood depicted Midwestern American life with precise forms and carefully organized compositions. His art often combines regional identity with irony and stylization.
artists.context: American Gothic uses frontality, repeated verticals and a distinctive architectural backdrop.

editorialNote: Concise introductory curatorial summaries; approximate dates and activity periods are used where appropriate. Timeline sorting uses an approximate birth or activity year, not a definitive chronology. Selected institutional references are provided; remaining profiles are editorial summaries pending full scholarly review.

science.name: Antoine and Marie-Anne Lavoisier
science.summary: Their collaboration helped transform chemistry into a quantitative experimental discipline. Marie-Anne translated scientific work and produced illustrations of apparatus for the 1789 chemistry textbook. David’s double portrait connects scientific instruments with the public identity of the researchers.

science.name: Isaac Newton
science.summary: Newton formulated laws of motion and universal gravitation and made major contributions to optics and mathematics. The Kneller portrait presents Newton as a historical person, whereas Blake uses him as a symbolic figure to explore the limits of rational measurement.

science.name: Albert Einstein
science.summary: Einstein developed special and general relativity, reshaping the understanding of space, time and gravity. His work on the photoelectric effect also helped establish quantum physics and was singled out in the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics. The two portraits document distinct artistic interpretations of the same physicist.

science.name: Nikola Tesla
science.summary: Tesla contributed to alternating-current power systems, including polyphase motors, and experimented with high-frequency electrical phenomena. His Blue Portrait offers an unusual point of contact between portraiture and electrically controlled illumination.
